hint.text:
Conditional 1
if-clause: if + simple present
main clause: will-future

Conditional 2
if-clause: if + simple past
main clause: would/could/might + infinitive

Conditional 3
if-clause: if + past perfect
main clause: would/could/might + have + past participle

instruction.text: Select the correct type of conditional sentence.

atoms.a: If she studies more regularly, she will pass the final exam.
atoms.b: ++type_1 type_2 type_3

feedback.wrong: Der Satz beschreibt eine realistische Bedingung in der Gegenwart.

atoms.a: If we lived in a bigger city, we would have more cultural opportunities.
atoms.b: type_1 ++type_2 type_3

feedback.wrong: Der Satz beschreibt eine unrealistische Bedingung in der Gegenwart.

atoms.a: If the government had acted earlier, the crisis could have been avoided.
atoms.b: type_1 type_2 ++type_3

feedback.wrong: Der Satz beschreibt eine unmögliche Bedingung in der Vergangenheit.

atoms.a: They will miss the beginning of the film if they don't hurry.
atoms.b: ++type_1 type_2 type_3

feedback.wrong: Der Satz beschreibt eine realistische Bedingung in der Gegenwart.

atoms.a: I would change the company's strategy if I was in charge.
atoms.b: type_1 ++type_2 type_3

atoms.b: type_1 type_2 ++type_3

instruction.text: Fill in the gap of the main clause, using the right conditional.

instruction.text: Fill in the gap of the if-clause, using the right conditional.

atoms.b: If we ((don't_take --didn't_take --hadn't_taken)) immediate action, the damage to the ecosystem will become irreversible.
The economy would recover faster if governments ((--reduce reduced --had_reduced)) bureaucracy for small businesses.
If we ((--notice --noticed had_noticed)) the early signs of his sickness, we could have provided better support for him.
The technicians will resolve any technical problems immediately if we ((++encounter encountered had_encountered)) them during the live event.
She would feel more at ease in the new environment if someone ((shows ++showed had_shown)) her around on the first day.
If we ((take took ++hadn’t_taken)) that wrong turn, we would have arrived long before sunset.
If she ever ((decides --decided --had_decided)) to publish her novel, many readers will relate to her story.
If the city council ((--offers offered --had_offered)) more affordable housing, young families would consider staying in the area.
The scandal might have caused less damage if the company ((--reacts --reacted had_reacted)) transparently from the beginning.
